_rules: Vetoes are medical: classify on the safe side (Robin 2026-09-24)

A row is classed only on a stated ingredient: a published ingredient list, the maker's declaration, a 'may contain' label on the recommended bottle, or a book that names it. Never on a tasting note, a rumoured historical formula or 'secret recipe' alone (Robin 2026-10-06)
nutmeg, coconut, orgeat, amaretto, hazelnut liqueur, pine nuts -> nuts
undistilled beer/malt -> gluten; distilled grain spirits are NOT gluten
spice = heat only (bitters and baking spices are not spice)
wine fining agents ignored unless a named bottle is labelled

unknown ingredient -> the Mixologist adds it with scripts/add_ingredient.py, allergens on the safe side (every veto it could plausibly touch). His call, not Robin's: the guest's own veto protects them. The table follows the drink, never limits it (Robin 2026-09-25)

Sugar 29 g/100 ml DERIVED, not printed (Hester F23: Anís del Mono Dulce retailer label 35%, 308 kcal/100 ml; ethanol ~193 kcal leaves ~29 g sugar; our arithmetic). Treat as unsourced; swept 25-35. Aniseed/star anise/fennel, sugar, neutral spirit: no veto (spice = heat only)

anis_seco.name: Spanish anís seco (dry anise spirit, 40-50%)
anis_seco.source: Spain RD 164/2014 art. 6 (Hester F20-F21): a seco may carry up to 50 g/l sugar and 1-3 g/l essential oils. 0 g used as the dry end, unsourced; swept 0-5 g and 40-50% in the room. Aniseed and neutral spirit: no veto

orange_half_slice.name: orange half-slice (garnish)
orange_half_slice.source: garnish only: a half-moon slice of fresh orange set in the glass; not modelled in balance

pineapple_piece.name: small piece of fresh pineapple (garnish)
pineapple_piece.source: garnish only: a small wedge of fresh (or tinned, drained) pineapple set in the glass; not modelled in balance

cherry_fresh.name: fresh cherry (garnish)
cherry_fresh.source: garnish only: one fresh sweet cherry, stalk on; stone fruit, not a nut (maraschino-style cherries are NOT this row: maraschino is classed nuts in this table)

mint_sprig_bruised.name: fresh mint sprig, lightly bruised and left in the glass
mint_sprig_bruised.source: herb sprig pressed lightly and set in the drink (the 1934 reader's way, Imbibe! pdf 244); scent and a little taste as it sits, no sugar, acid or strength; not modelled in balance

orange_wheel_muddled.name: fresh orange wheel, cut in eight and muddled (counted as the juice it releases)
orange_wheel_muddled.source: juice values from Liquid Intelligence ingredient table (fresh orange juice, pdf 140-141); the ml a muddled wheel releases (about 15 ml from a 1 cm wheel of a medium orange) is my unsourced estimate, swept 10-20 ml; the peel's oils carry aroma, not sugar or acid. Method: Oxford BRONX COCKTAIL pdf 358

coriander_seed.name: coriander seeds, lightly cracked (shaken with the drink, fine-strained out)
coriander_seed.source: spice seed, muddled and shaken for aroma and fine-strained out; not modelled in balance (unsourced). Pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 80 (coriander seeds listed as a substitute for citrus); Oxford GIN pdf 894 (coriander for its lemony notes)

bourbon_blantons.name: Blanton's Original Single Barrel bourbon (46.5%)
bourbon_blantons.source: 93 proof, 46.5%: Breaking Bourbon review, 2021 (secondary, enthusiast site; Hester r3, card F19-F24); straight bourbon, no sugar or acid (LI pdf 140 note); distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

caramel_syrup.name: caramel syrup (sugar cooked in a pan to deep amber, then dissolved in hot water; about 70 Brix)
caramel_syrup.source: Liquid Intelligence ingredient table p. 137 (pdf 141): '70 Brix caramel syrup' at 61.5% sugar, 'sweetness is low because of sugar breakdown during caramelization—a guess'; method after LI p. 347 (pdf 351), scaled for home without a refractometer: my arithmetic, unsourced. Plain white sugar and water only

rosemary_syrup.name: fresh rosemary syrup (1:1, rosemary sprigs steeped in hot simple syrup, strained)
rosemary_syrup.source: sugar as 1:1 simple syrup (Liquid Intelligence table, same basis as mint_syrup); rosemary adds scent and taste, no sugar or acid (unsourced craft standard)

gin_london_dry_40.name: London dry gin at 40% (strength-sweep row)
gin_london_dry_40.source: Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note: straight spirits = label ABV, no sugar; 40% is the common lower bottling strength

rosemary_sprig.name: fresh rosemary sprig (garnish, for scent)
rosemary_sprig.source: garnish: scent only, no sugar, acid or strength counted

tomato_juice.name: tomato juice (bottled, plain; not a seasoned Bloody Mary mix)
tomato_juice.source: unsourced standard value (plain bottled tomato juice ~2.5-3.6 g sugars/100 ml, ~0.35-0.45% titratable acid as citric; my knowledge); no tomato row in LI's table (pp. 136-137)

manzanilla.name: manzanilla sherry (or any fino)
manzanilla.source: unsourced standard value, as the fino row (bone-dry, ~15%); Codex p. 221 suggests manzanilla in a Bloody Mary 'to up the savory ante'. Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4)

celery_salt.name: celery salt, a small pinch, shaken into the drink
celery_salt.source: ground celery seed and salt; seasoning only, not modelled in balance. Celery is not in the AD-4 veto enum (egg-white, dairy, gluten, nuts, spice); no heat, so not spice

cherry_heering.name: Cherry Heering (Danish cherry liqueur, 24%)
cherry_heering.source: ABV 24%: label (unsourced in the library). Sugar ~25 g/100 ml: back-calculated by Tomás from Liquid Intelligence's Blood and Sand (p. 133: start 90 ml at 12.3 g/100 ml; LI table sweet vermouth 16%, orange 12.4%), so an estimate on an estimate (Arnold calls liqueur sugars educated guesses, pdf 140). Allergen nuts on the safe side, Tomás's call: a cherry liqueur whose stones may be crushed in with the fruit (unsourced), same call as maraschino in this table. | RULED none (Tomás 2026-10-06, under Robin's evidence rule, D1): no page names stones or kernels for Cherry Heering. Oxford CHERRY BRANDY pdf 445-446 files Heering as the cherry-flavoured kind (cherries macerated in a spirit, or cherry juice, then sweetened; today on neutral spirit), and gives cracked pits only for true cherry brandy (kirsch) and maraschino, which stay nuts. The earlier safe-side call is kept above for the record; it goes back to nuts if a maker's list or label names stones.

coffee_beans_whole.name: whole roasted coffee beans (garnish, floated; not ground, not brewed)
coffee_beans_whole.source: garnish only, nothing measurable enters the drink; floating on a shaken sour is unsourced (Tomás's craft knowledge). Coffee touches no studio veto (not nuts, dairy, gluten, egg or heat)

madeira_rainwater.name: rainwater Madeira
madeira_rainwater.source: Barbeito Rainwater 3 Anos producer's sheet (secondary, one bottle, Hester explorer-innocent r3-r4): 18.27% ABV, 5.8 g/100 ml sugar, total acidity 6.46 (units not printed; read as g/L tartaric = 0.65%), used as the style's representative; swept 2-8 g and 0.5-0.9%. Rainwater is defined by colour and sweetness (1.0-2.5 deg Baume), Portaria 38/2015. Wine: fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4)

orange_curacao.name: orange curaçao (dry-style, brandy-based)
orange_curacao.source: unsourced: 40% typical (Pierre Ferrand Dry Curaçao, the Imbibe! pdf 217 pick, label not on a page); sugar taken as LI's Cointreau (25 g/100 ml, pp. 136-137), swept 20-35 g and 30-40%

caol_ila_12.name: Caol Ila 12 Islay single malt Scotch whisky (43%)
caol_ila_12.source: label ABV 43% (Diageo US, Systembolaget 37701, LCBO 602029, fetched 2026-10-01; Hester F23, magician-regular-guy); straight spirit: no sugar, minimal acid (LI pdf 140 note); distilled grain (malted barley) spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); no labelled fining

irish_pot_still_whiskey.name: Irish single pot still whiskey (style, 40%+)
irish_pot_still_whiskey.source: style floor 40% (the legal minimum; common bottlings 40-46%, unsourced); straight spirit (LI pdf 140 note); distilled grain spirit (malted and unmalted barley), not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

demerara_sugar.name: demerara sugar (loose)
demerara_sugar.source: pure cane sugar; dissolved volume 0.63 ml per g (as sugar_cube; LI 0.62 ml/g); ~4 g per level teaspoon (unsourced)

red_wine_young_spanish.name: young unoaked Spanish red wine (joven: Tempranillo or Garnacha style)
red_wine_young_spanish.source: unsourced standard values: ABV 13% (joven reds run ~12.5-14%, own knowledge); sugar and acid as LI's dry red (Cabernet row, pdf 140-141). Style from Creasey, Guardian 2012 (fact card F10: the house wine is the one you mix) and Codex p. 18 (no grand wine). Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4); sulphites have no veto.

coca_cola.name: Coca-Cola (full-sugar cola)
coca_cola.source: unsourced: sugar 10.6 g/100 ml is Coca-Cola Original Taste's label value (own knowledge, not read on a page this session); acid ~0.05% phosphoric, own estimate (Codex p. 194: phosphoric acid gives most of a commercial soda's acidity). Allergens: carbonated water, sugar, caramel colour, phosphoric acid, natural flavourings, caffeine: none on the veto list; caffeine is not a veto. Caramel colour: the maker states its colas gluten-free (own knowledge, unsourced); no gluten class. RECLASSIFIED nuts (Tomás, outlaw-jester r3, 2026-10-01), safe side: two published historical 7X formulas (Beal notebook, Atlanta Journal-Constitution 1979; Pemberton notebook via Pendergrast; both via This American Life 'The Recipe') list nutmeg oil; Coca-Cola denies they are the formula (Reuters via NBC, 2011); today's recipe is secret; nutmeg counts as nuts (Robin). Hester fact card lord-invader-rum-and-coca-cola C1-C2. Affects innocent-creator (The Way It Felt): note to Robin. | RULED none (Robin 2026-10-06, collection review D1/D8): a row is classed only on a stated ingredient (a published ingredient list, the maker's declaration, a 'may contain' label on the recommended bottle, or a book naming the ingredient), never on a tasting note, a rumoured historical formula or 'secret recipe' alone; the earlier safe-side reasoning is kept above for the record. Basis here: rumoured historical formulas only.

kalimotxo_ice.name: ice cubes frozen from equal parts young Spanish red and Coca-Cola
kalimotxo_ice.source: computed: equal parts of red_wine_young_spanish and coca_cola (volume contraction ignored). Counted as melted in the spec: it melts into the same composition. Freezes in a home freezer: LI p. 141 (a mix freezes if under 15.5% ABV and 9 g/100 ml sugar; this is 6.5% and 5.4 g).

ginger_ale.name: ginger ale (commercial, pale dry style, sweetened, non-alcoholic)
ginger_ale.source: unsourced standard values (typical pale dry label ~8.5-9.5 g sugar/100 ml; acid estimated). Gingerol is 'a relative of capsaicin' (Flavor Matrix pdf 132): heat, spice on the safe side

zirbenz.name: Zirbenz Stone Pine Liqueur of the Alps (recommended; or any Alpine stone-pine liqueur, Zirbenlikör)
zirbenz.source: ABV: importer's product page and 2026 catalogue p. 12 (35.0%). Sugar UNSOURCED design value 15 g/100 ml: EU liqueur floor 100 g/L (Reg. (EU) 2019/787, my own knowledge, unverified here); an unvetted web page claims 120 g/L but also 38% ABV against the label's 35%, so not used; swept 10-30 in hero-explorer. Allergens: made by steeping the young whole cones of the Arolla stone pine (importer catalogue, PUNCH 2015; de.wikipedia: cones sliced 3-5 mm, 5-6 weeks in grain spirit); the seeds inside are pine nuts (en.wikipedia Pinus cembra) -> nuts (STUDIO-RULES 4). Applies to every stone-pine liqueur.

allspice_dram.name: allspice dram (pimento dram; e.g. St. Elizabeth style)
allspice_dram.source: Oxford PIMENTO DRAM pdf 1513: allspice (Pimenta dioica) berries extracted with high-proof spirit, most often rum, plus sugar and lime juice; flavour 'reminiscent of' cloves, cinnamon and nutmeg (a resemblance, not nutmeg). ABV 22.5% (St. Elizabeth label, my own knowledge, unsourced); sugar 25 g/100 ml and acid 0.2% unsourced estimates (importer: 'without excess sugar'). Allspice is a baking spice, not heat: no spice veto. Swept in hero-explorer (tiny dose).

pineau_des_charentes_blanc.name: Pineau des Charentes (blanc)
pineau_des_charentes_blanc.source: Codex p. 74; Oxford MISTELLE pdf 1314-1315, PINEAU pdf 1518 (16-22%). ABV 17.5 within the sourced band. Sugar 13 g/100 ml: above the AOC control-plan floor of 120 g/L for white Pineau (INAO/Qualisud PCPineau/P300-8, via Hester, innocent-explorer r4); exact typical value unsourced. Acid 0.45%: unsourced standard value (EU single document gives no minimum total acidity).

cognac_sichuan_pepper.name: cognac steeped with Sichuan peppercorns (strained)
cognac_sichuan_pepper.source: cognac as LI (41%); Sichuan peppercorn adds aroma and tingle only, no sugar/acid (unsourced); spice on the safe side: a guest avoiding heat would reasonably fear a peppercorn (Matrix pdf 140 pairs it with grape)

apricot_steeped_rye.name: straight rye whiskey steeped with dried apricots, strained (60 g chopped dried apricots per 250 ml rye, room temperature, 6-8 hours)
apricot_steeped_rye.source: Tomás estimate, unsourced: rye at the table's 50% (LI pdf 140) less ~4% for fruit water; dried apricot ~53% sugar by mass (unsourced USDA-style value), ~30% of it extracted into ~240 ml recovered = ~4 g/100 ml; fruit acid ~0.15%. Ratio from Codex p. 99 (dried fruit 1:4 by weight). nuts on the safe side: dried fruit is commonly packed alongside nuts, and apricot kernels are an almond stand-in (stone fruit and almonds botanically related, Codex p. 37) | RULED none (Tomás 2026-10-06, under Robin's evidence rule, D1/check 4): no stated ingredient. 'Dried fruit is commonly packed alongside nuts' has no source (Hester searched the library and the web, applied/_hester.md), and Codex p. 37's 'botanically related' is a flavour note; only the dried flesh is steeped, no kernel. The earlier safe-side call is kept above for the record. A 'may contain nuts' label on the guest's own pack still applies: the recipe note tells a nut-allergic maker to check it.

abbey_ale.name: malty Belgian-style abbey ale (dubbel style, low hops, about 6.5-8%)
abbey_ale.source: Counted as Arnold counts it: his Red-Hot Ale stats (LI pdf 191: 3.5 g/100 ml sugar, 0.33% acid) come from the syrup and lemon alone, so the ale's own sugar and acid are about nil in his arithmetic; ABV 7% unsourced (dubbel style, 6.5-8%); Ommegang Abbey Ale named there. Worst case swept at the table's 'beer' values (1 g, 0.3%).

dry_cider.name: dry (brut) hard apple cider, still or lightly sparkling, about 5-6.5%
dry_cider.source: unsourced standard values (dry cider ~0.5-2 g/100 ml residual sugar, titratable acid ~0.3-0.6% as malic); Arnold's Red-Hot Cider stats (LI pdf 192) count the cider's sugar and acid as about nil, so this row is stricter than his; swept in explorer-jester

red_bordeaux.name: young red Bordeaux (claret: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot blend, dry)
red_bordeaux.source: sugar and acid as Liquid Intelligence's dry red (Cabernet Sauvignon row, pdf 140-141); ABV 13.5% unsourced standard value (young Bordeaux reds run ~12.5-14.5%, own knowledge). Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4); no named bottle.

rye_40.name: straight rye whiskey at 40% (80 proof)
rye_40.source: unsourced standard value: US straight rye bottled at the 80-proof floor; distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

borovicka.name: borovička (juniper spirit, 'the Czechoslovak version of gin'; a style, no brand)
borovicka.source: Oxford pdf 1710: 'borovička, the Czechoslovak version of gin'; ABV 40% unsourced standard value (labels run about 37.5-40%); distilled, so no gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); no sugar or acid as a straight spirit (LI pdf 140)

mango_syrup.name: blended mango syrup (equal weights ripe peeled mango flesh and white sugar, blended cold until smooth, pressed through a fine sieve; fridge, up to 2 weeks; method of Cocktail Codex p. 47, Blended Strawberry Syrup)
mango_syrup.source: method Codex pp. 46-47; values unsourced standard estimate: mango flesh ~14 g sugar/100 g and ~0.4% acid, halved by the sugar, density ~1.27. contains nuts ON THE SAFE SIDE: mango is in the cashew and pistachio family and cross-reactions are reported (unsourced, Tomás's call)

rich_syrup.name: rich simple syrup (2:1 by weight)
rich_syrup.source: Liquid Intelligence p. 51: rich simple is 2 parts sugar to 1 part water by weight; 200 g sugar (~124 ml at LI 0.62 ml/g) + 100 g water ~ 224 ml -> ~89 g/100 ml (computed)

creme_de_mure.name: crème de mûre (blackberry liqueur)
creme_de_mure.source: PROVISIONAL, unsourced: EU 'crème de' liqueur floor of 250 g sugar per litre (my knowledge, Regulation 2019/787) used at the floor; ABV 16% typical (15-20%). Sweep against crème de cassis (40 g, 16%) as the sweet bound. Blackberry only: no nut, dairy or grain declared; any added flavouring to be checked per named bottle.

rum_zacapa_23.name: Ron Zacapa 23 aged rum (recommended; or any aged Spanish-style rum, not spiced, about 40%)
rum_zacapa_23.source: label 40% (secondary: Caskers and Flaviar, 'may vary' by market; Hester jester-explorer r5); sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note; any added sugar is unsourced and swept 0-2 g/100 ml in jester-explorer; Codex p. 109 names it for Old-Fashioned riffs, with an affinity for rye from its former whiskey barrels (this bottle's, not the style's)

balsamic_vinegar.name: balsamic vinegar (aceto balsamico di Modena style, not a glaze)
balsamic_vinegar.source: unsourced standard values: acidity 6% (my knowledge of the Modena IGP minimum); sugar ~20 g/100 ml estimate from cooked grape must (swept 10-35). Grape must and wine vinegar only: no veto. Thickened glazes can carry starch, so the recipe says vinegar, not glaze.

blackberry_fresh.name: fresh blackberry (garnish)
blackberry_fresh.source: garnish, no measurable contribution; Proper p. 31 / Oxford BRAMBLE pdf 336 garnish

lemon_wedge.name: lemon wedge (garnish)
lemon_wedge.source: garnish, no measurable contribution; Proper p. 31

borovicka_sweet2.name: borovička at 40% with 2 g sugar/100 ml (sweep row: Spišská GI lists invert sugar, amount not given)
borovicka_sweet2.source: sweep row, hypothetical sugar; Spišská borovička GI dossier (via Hester) lists liquid invert sugar, no amount

borovicka_sweet4.name: borovička at 40% with 4 g sugar/100 ml (sweep row: Spišská GI lists invert sugar, amount not given)
borovicka_sweet4.source: sweep row, hypothetical sugar; Spišská borovička GI dossier (via Hester) lists liquid invert sugar, no amount

cacao_nib_tincture_gin.name: cacao nib tincture, made in the gin (10 g cacao nibs per 100 ml London dry gin, steeped, strained)
cacao_nib_tincture_gin.source: Codex printed 297: Cacao Nib Tincture, 75 g nibs per 750 ml vodka, iSi-infused, refrigerate up to 4 weeks; Codex p. 89 calls it chocolatey (but dry). Home version in the gin, steeped not pressure-infused: Tomás's craft call, unsourced; ABV taken as the gin's (unsourced). Allergens on the safe side: cacao products often carry shared-plant nut and milk warnings | RULED none (Tomás 2026-10-06, under Robin's evidence rule, D1/D8): the tincture is cacao nibs and gin only, and no maker's list or read label names nuts or milk; 'shared-plant warnings' were a generalisation, not a label. Aligned with creme_de_cacao_white (none). Recipe note where used: 'If you have a nut or milk allergy, check the nibs' pack for a warning.' Back to nuts/dairy if the recommended nibs' label says may contain.

bay_leaf_dried.name: dried bay leaf, torn in half, left in the glass
bay_leaf_dried.source: kitchen-shelf dried bay (laurel); Flavor Matrix lists laurel on its Citrus wheel (pdf 81, printed 71) and Grape wheel (pdf 141, printed 131), both rendered and read. Scent and a little taste; no sugar, acid or strength (Tomás's craft call). Touches no studio veto: not a nut, dairy, gluten, egg, and not heat

maple_syrup.name: maple syrup (grade B / dark, robust)
maple_syrup.source: Liquid Intelligence ingredient table, pdf 141 (printed 137): maple syrup 87.5% sweetness, 0% acid; pdf 57 (p. 53): ~67% sugar by weight, 1 oz maple as sweet as 1.5 oz simple

bourbon_four_roses_bentons.name: Four Roses bourbon (40%) washed with Benton's bacon fat (1 1/2 oz melted fat per 750 ml, 4 h room temperature, 2 h freezer, fat lifted off, strained)
bourbon_four_roses_bentons.source: Recipe and wash ratio: A Proper Drink pp. 275-276 (Lee's printed recipe: 'Four Roses bourbon'); 40%: UNSOURCED (my value; the US minimum bottling strength). Only 'Yellow Label' is on record, as Lee's word in PUNCH 2019 (Hester F21), and no page gives its proof (Hester r5). Strength and sugar assumed unchanged by the wash (unsourced, my craft call). SPICE on the safe side: Benton's bacon is dry-cured with salt, brown sugar and black pepper (maker's page, Hester F26); black pepper's pungency is heat (my knowledge, unsourced), and a fat wash exists to carry the fat's flavour into the spirit (Codex p. 94), so lifting the fat off doesn't prove the pepper left. Precedent: cognac_sichuan_pepper. Pork: not a veto, but closed to anyone who doesn't eat pork.

shackleton_blended_malt.name: Shackleton blended malt Scotch whisky (40%, no age statement), named for him and built on a recreation of the whisky his expedition left under its 1908 hut
shackleton_blended_malt.source: ABV 40%: The Spirits Business and scotchwhisky.com (April 2017), via Hester's card shackleton-nimrod-mackinlays.md (explorer-ruler r2); trade press, not the brand's site. Not the hut whisky and not the 2011 replica (limited 50,000 bottles, Antarctic Heritage Trust / CBC-AP 19 Jan 2013). Straight spirit: no sugar, minimal acid (LI pdf 140 note). Distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); no labelled fining known

scotch_blended_malt.name: blended malt Scotch whisky (style; malts only, no grain whisky), 40% or stronger
scotch_blended_malt.source: style floor 40% (the legal minimum for Scotch; blended malts commonly 40-46%, unsourced). Straight spirit (LI pdf 140 note). Distilled grain (malted barley) spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

plum_syrup.name: rich plum syrup (100 g ripe plums, stoned, blended smooth with 200 g white sugar, warmed gently only until the sugar dissolves, pressed through a fine sieve; fridge, about a week; adapted from the Cocktail Codex's Blended Strawberry Syrup, p. 47, at twice its sugar)
plum_syrup.source: method adapted from the Codex's Blended Strawberry Syrup (p. 47: equal weights, blended cold, sieved); here plums, 2 parts sugar to 1 of fruit, warmed to dissolve: Tomás's own adaptation. Values UNSOURCED estimate by Tomás: ripe plum ~9.9 g sugar/100 g and ~0.6-1.0% titratable acid (malic); 200 g sugar ~124 ml (LI 0.62 ml/g, pp. 136-137) + 100 g purée ~100 ml = ~224 ml -> 93.7 g sugar/100 ml, acid 0.45% at the sharp end (0.27% at 0.6%). Allergens: fresh stone-fruit flesh, not a nut (as cherry_fresh); the stones come out whole and are never cracked, since kernels are classed nuts (as creme_de_noyaux)

espresso.name: espresso, freshly pulled
espresso.source: Liquid Intelligence p. 137 (pdf 141) table: Espresso 0.0% alcohol, 0.0% sugar, 1.50% acid. Coffee touches no studio veto

brandy_aged_grape.name: brandy (aged grape brandy, e.g. a VS cognac or Spanish brandy)
brandy_aged_grape.source: Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note: straight spirits = label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid (40% typical label). Some brandies are sweetened or coloured with caramel (allowed in cognac): unsourced, my knowledge; numbers assume an unsweetened bottle

saline_solution.name: saline solution (20% salt in water, by weight)
saline_solution.source: Liquid Intelligence p. 61 (pdf 65): Arnold's saline; any cocktail with coffee benefits from a pinch of salt, kept below the point you'd taste it

parsnip_syrup.name: roasted parsnip syrup (250 g parsnip roasted until browned, simmered 10 min with 250 g sugar and 250 ml water, strained; about 400 ml, fridge)
parsnip_syrup.source: Pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 224 (root vegetables: celery root, parsnip, salsify; best pairings include coffee and bourbon; most commonly roasted or boiled). Sugar 62 g/100 ml and acid 0.1% are unsourced estimates (250 g sugar in about 400 ml strained syrup, my arithmetic). Parsnip is in the carrot/celery family: no studio veto (celery not in the enum), same flag as caraway

glenlivet_12.name: The Glenlivet 12 Year Old Speyside single malt Scotch whisky (recommended; or any unpeated Speyside single malt, not sherry-cask)
glenlivet_12.source: ABV 40%: unsourced label value (Scotch legal minimum; check the bottle, some markets 40-43%). Straight spirit, no sugar or acid (LI pdf 140 note). Character: Oxford GLENLIVET pdf 918 'subtle, even delicate'; Codex p. 204 'elegant and floral, with a touch of honey'. Distilled malted-barley spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4).

gin_tanqueray_london_dry_431.name: Tanqueray London Dry gin (43.1%, UK/EU bottling)
gin_tanqueray_london_dry_431.source: label ABV 43.1% for the UK/EU bottling (unsourced, my knowledge; strength differs by market); unsweetened as a London dry (Oxford LONDON DRY GIN pdf 1191). Botanicals purportedly juniper, coriander, angelica, licorice (Oxford TANQUERAY GORDON & CO. pdf 1986). Distilled grain spirit: not gluten (rules).

gin_tanqueray_london_dry_473.name: Tanqueray London Dry gin (47.3%, US bottling)
gin_tanqueray_london_dry_473.source: label ABV 47.3% for the US bottling (unsourced, my knowledge); otherwise as gin_tanqueray_london_dry_431

licorice_root_syrup.name: licorice root syrup (1:1 simple syrup, 100 g sugar + 100 ml water, with 5 g dried licorice root, chopped, simmered 5 minutes, steeped off the heat 30 minutes, strained; about 160 ml, fridge)
licorice_root_syrup.source: sugar taken as LI simple syrup 61.5 g/100 ml (pdf 140-141); the short simmer's evaporation and the root's own sugars and glycyrrhizin sweetness are not counted (unsourced; glycyrrhizin tastes far sweeter than sucrose, so this syrup reads sweeter than its grams: dose it at the low end). Allergens: licorice root is a legume, kin to peanut, and dried roots are often packed alongside nuts: nuts on the safe side (Tomás's call, like dried fruit and cacao nibs).

rum_gold_puerto_rican.name: gold Puerto Rican rum (lightly aged, style)
rum_gold_puerto_rican.source: LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note; 40% typical label (unsourced); the style Berry printed, Oxford ZOMBIE pdf 2229

rum_gold_jamaican.name: gold Jamaican rum (aged, style)
rum_gold_jamaican.source: LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note; 40% typical label (unsourced), swept 40-46%; the style Berry printed, Oxford ZOMBIE pdf 2229

rum_lemon_hart_151.source: 151 US proof = 75.5% ABV (arithmetic); named in Berry's printed Zombie, Oxford ZOMBIE pdf 2229; sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 note (unsourced for this bottle)

gin_tanqueray_london_dry_413.name: Tanqueray London Dry gin (41.3%, UK bottling)

bonal.name: Bonal Gentiane-Quina (French gentian-and-cinchona aperitif wine, 16%)

Sugar 12 g/100 ml and acid 0.5% UNSOURCED estimates, swept 6-18 g and 0.3-0.7% in the pour's checks. Wine: fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4). Gentian and cinchona are bitters, not heat: no spice.

mandarin_liqueur.name: mandarin liqueur (brandy-based, Mandarine Napoléon style)
mandarin_liqueur.source: UNSOURCED: 38% typical of the brandy-based style; sugar 25 g/100 ml estimated as an orange liqueur (cf. LI's Cointreau 25), swept 18-35 g and 30-40% in the pour's checks. Jimmie Charters names 'Mandarin' in his Dingo cocktail (This Must Be the Place, p. 83, OCR highlight, Hester). Citrus peel and brandy: no veto.

canadian_whisky.name: Canadian whisky (blended, 40%)
canadian_whisky.source: Oxford Companion, WHISKY, CANADIAN pdf 2146: by law not less than 40% ABV, may include caramel colouring and flavouring; pdf 2147: provincial taxes keep most at the legal minimum. Sugar 0 unsourced (flavouring allowed; treated as a straight spirit per LI pdf 140). Distilled grain spirit: not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); no veto on the safe side (flavourings are typically wine or spirit, unsourced)

canadian_whisky_45.name: Canadian whisky, higher-proof sipping style (45%), sweep only

mandarin_peel.name: mandarin peel (strip; a clementine works)
mandarin_peel.source: garnish: peel oils only, no sugar/acid/strength counted. Citrus peel: no veto.

giffard_triple_sec.name: Giffard Triple Sec (25%, the classic bottling)
giffard_triple_sec.source: 25%: giffard.com product page (Hester F24, 2026-10-01). Sugar NOT published (Giffard: 'sweetened with sugar or honey (100g/L min)'); 25 g/100 ml is a STAND-IN, Cointreau's LI value (pp. 136-137). Swept 10-40 g: in range from 20 g up.

sloe_gin.name: sloe gin (British style: blackthorn berries steeped in sweetened gin; about 26%)
sloe_gin.source: ABV ~26%: label strength of the common British style (unsourced, e.g. Plymouth Sloe Gin's label; commercial range ~20-30%, swept). Sugar ~20 g/100 ml: back-calculated by Tomás from Liquid Intelligence's Blackthorn (p. 131: 45 ml Plymouth gin 41.2%, 22.5 ml sweet vermouth 16%, 22.5 ml sloe gin, start 91.6 ml at 8.9 g/100 ml), an estimate on an estimate (Arnold calls liqueur sugars educated guesses, pdf 140). Acid 0%: derived by Tomás (regular-guy-sage r3, 2026-10-01) from Liquid Intelligence p. 131, the same Blackthorn the sugar comes from: its start acid of 0.15% is supplied by its 22.5 ml of sweet vermouth alone (0.6%), so Arnold's model gives the sloe gin about 0. Was 0.5% (Tomás's unsourced guess, outlaw-explorer). Swept 0-0.2%; outlaw-explorer's Whoopee moves from 0.90% to 0.75% finished acid (edge), noted for Robin. Allergens: nuts, on the safe side (Hester, outlaw-explorer r3, card _studio/fact-cards/sloe-gin.md): Difford's Guide says some makers crush the stones and steep again for almond notes, or add crushed almonds; Sipsmith notes 19th-century recipes added a crushed almond or a few crushed stones; a 2010 tasting found almond/marzipan notes in sold bottles. An unnamed style can't rule either out (same call as maraschino, Codex p. 174). Back to veto-free only for a named bottle whose maker states no cracked stones and no added almond. Sugar figure is derived (LI table's sweet vermouth at 16 g; LI doesn't name its vermouth) and swept 15-30 g.

cynar.name: Cynar (Italian artichoke-based bitter liqueur, 16.5%)
cynar.source: Artichoke-based amaro: Oxford Companion, FLOC DE GASCOGNE (pdf 822). ABV 16.5%: label (unsourced in the library). Sugar ~18 g/100 ml: unsourced estimate by Tomás (moderately sweet Italian amaro; LI's table has Campari at 24). Recipe secret: no nut, dairy or heat ingredient on any page; classified veto-free like Campari

hudson_rye.name: Hudson New York straight rye whiskey (46%; the line Oxford calls Hudson Manhattan Rye, 92 proof, 100% New York rye)
hudson_rye.source: Oxford HUDSON pdf 1037: 92-proof, 100 percent New York rye; current label name and strength to be confirmed (Hester); distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

apple_brandy_40.name: American apple brandy at 40% (80 proof)
apple_brandy_40.source: unsourced standard value: American apple brandy at the 80-proof floor, for the substitute sweep

hudson_do_the_rye_thing.name: Hudson Do The Rye Thing New York straight rye whiskey (46%; 95% rye, 5% malted barley; the line formerly Hudson Manhattan Rye)
hudson_do_the_rye_thing.source: Hester T2: The Spirits Business 15 Sep 2020 (renamed from Manhattan Rye, new recipe 95% rye / 5% malted barley); maker's site fetched 2026-10-01 (New York straight rye, 46%). Distilled grain spirit incl. malted barley, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

sweet_vermouth_cardamom.name: sweet vermouth steeped with green cardamom (about 3 g whole pods per 250 ml, room temperature, about 12 hours, strained)
sweet_vermouth_cardamom.source: values as sweet_vermouth (Liquid Intelligence pdf 140-141); a whole-pod steep adds no sugar or acid (unsourced, my call). Steep after Cocktail Codex p. 95 (vermouth infuses slowly; cardamom is delicate, ~12 h) and p. 288 (Cardamom-Infused St-Germain, 10 g pods per 750 ml, room temperature, about 12 hours). Cardamom is not heat, so not spice (rule 4)

cachaca_unaged.name: unaged (white, prata) cachaça
cachaca_unaged.source: Codex p. 112: cachaça is distilled once from Brazilian sugarcane juice to 38-48% ABV; white = unaged or rested in neutral containers. 40% is a representative bottling (unsourced); swept 38-48. Distilled cane spirit: no veto

ogogoro_pedros.name: Pedro's Premium Ògógóró, unaged (40%; not the 5-year aged bottling), palm-sap spirit redistilled in Lagos
ogogoro_pedros.source: ABV: Difford's Guide 'Pedro's Ògógóró' (alc./vol 40%, unaged) and Artifex Drinks product page (40% ABV), both fetched 2026-10-01; sugar and acid unsourced (unaged straight spirit, LI pdf 140 note)

apricot_eau_de_vie.name: apricot eau-de-vie (clear, unsweetened apricot brandy: barack pálinka or Marillenbrand style)
apricot_eau_de_vie.source: Oxford APRICOT BRANDY pdf 133: a true eau-de-vie, clear, 'little residual sugar' (0 g used, unsourced approximation); 40% typical bottling strength unsourced. nuts on the safe side: a stone fruit's pit holds a kernel (Flavor Matrix pdf 236), and amaretto 'is generally made from apricot kernels' (Oxford ALMOND LIQUEURS pdf 94; amaretto is nuts in the studio rules); Codex p. 37 says only that stone fruit and almond are botanically related; fruit spirits may be distilled with the stones (my knowledge, unsourced) | RULED none (Tomás 2026-10-06, under Robin's evidence rule, D1/check 4): no page names kernels or stones as an ingredient of apricot eau-de-vie. Oxford APRICOT BRANDY pdf 133 makes it from 'apricots and apricot pomace'; ABRICOTINE pdf 47's 'a touch of almond' is a tasting note; amaretto's apricot kernels (pdf 94) are another product; Matrix pdf 236 and Codex p. 37 are botany; 'distilled with the stones' was my own knowledge. Contrast kirsch, which stays nuts: Oxford pdf 1135, 'distilled from cherries and their pits'. Back to nuts if a recommended bottle's label or a page names the stones.

apricot_flavoured_brandy.name: apricot-flavoured brandy (sweet apricot liqueur, e.g. the Bols / DeKuyper style)
apricot_flavoured_brandy.source: Oxford APRICOT BRANDY pdf 133: neutral spirit or brandy with apricot juice and sweeteners, 'more reasonably... apricot liqueur'. 24% / 30 g / 0.2% unsourced standard values. nuts on the safe side (kernel flavour; Oxford pdf 94: amaretto is generally made from apricot kernels). Added only to prove why the recipe says eau-de-vie, not liqueur | RULED none (Tomás 2026-10-06, D1/check 4): 'kernel flavour' is a tasting note, and pdf 133 lists apricot juice, sweeteners and natural flavors, no kernel. Used by no spec (sweep row only).

sugar_rim_fine.name: fine (caster) sugar on the outside of the rim
sugar_rim_fine.source: plain sucrose on the glass's outside rim (Regan, Joy pdf 137: exterior only, so it stays out of the drink); eaten at the lip, not dissolved, so not modelled in balance

jeppsons_malort.name: Jeppson's Malört (bitter wormwood liqueur, besk style; CH Distillery, Chicago)
jeppsons_malort.source: 35% ALC/VOL: maker's product page and Kleinman, Drink Spirits (Hester, card B2). Sugar: no maker's figure; modelled at the US liqueur legal floor, 2.5% sugar by weight (27 CFR 5.150) ~ 2.4 g/100 ml (Hester's arithmetic); swept 2.4-6 in the pour. Colour FD&C Yellow No. 5 (no veto class). Wormwood liqueur on a distilled base: no veto class (distilled spirits aren't gluten, STUDIO-RULES 4)

armagnac.source: Oxford ARMAGNAC pdf 137-140 (grape brandy, Gascony); Codex pp. 157-158 (blended VS/VSOP for mixing); 40% = label floor, unsourced standard value; LI pdf 140 note: straight spirits, no sugar, minimal acid

floc_de_gascogne_blanc.name: Floc de Gascogne (white)
floc_de_gascogne_blanc.source: Strength 17%: midpoint of the legal 16-18% at bottling (cahier des charges, via Hester, fact card floc-de-gascogne.md, outlaw-innocent r3); Oxford FLOC pdf 818 says 18-20. Sugar 13 g/100 ml: unsourced (the law sets only the must at >=170 g/L when the Armagnac goes in; must is 2/3-3/4 of the blend per Oxford, so ~11-13 g if unfermented, less if fermentation had begun). floc_syrup_1to1.source: computed: 100 g sugar ~62 ml (LI 0.62 ml/g) + 100 ml Floc = 162 ml; sugar (100 + 13)/162 = 69.8; ABV 17x100/162 = 10.5 (Floc at the legal 16-18%, midpoint); acid 0.45x100/162. Floc's sugar and acid unsourced

brandied_peach.name: brandied peach slice (canned or fresh peach soaked in brandy and a spoon of syrup)

raspberry_syrup.name: blended raspberry syrup (equal weights fresh raspberries and white sugar, blended cold until smooth, pressed through a fine sieve to take out the seeds; fridge, up to a week; method of Cocktail Codex p. 47, Blended Strawberry Syrup)

mint_leaves_left_in.name: fresh mint leaves (spearmint), whipped with the drink and left in the glass
mint_leaves_left_in.source: herb leaf, whipped with the drink and poured in with it (Cocktail Codex p. 134 Mojito method); scent and a little taste, no sugar, acid or strength; not modelled in balance

raspberry_fresh.name: fresh raspberry (garnish)
raspberry_fresh.source: whole fresh berry on top; not modelled

raspberry_cumin_syrup.source: method adapted from Codex pp. 46-47 (equal weights fruit and sugar, blended cold, sieved); the cumin and its dose are Tomás's craft call (Flavor Matrix pdf 52: cumin among berries' surprise pairings). Allergens: berry and seed spice, no veto class; cumin is not heat (spice = heat only, STUDIO-RULES 4); raspberry seeds sieved out, not nuts

rum_angostura_1919.name: Angostura 1919 aged Trinidad rum (40%), recommended, or any column-distilled aged rum, not spiced, about 40%

orange_marmalade.source: unsourced: ~60 g sugar per 100 g (typical label value for full-sugar marmalade) at ~1.3 g/ml = ~78 g per 100 ml; acid ~0.5% by mass (~0.6 per 100 ml) estimated. pineapple_juice_pressed.name: fresh pineapple, pressed in the mixing glass (its juice)
pineapple_juice_pressed.source: unsourced standard value for fresh pineapple juice (~10 g sugar/100 ml, ~0.8% acid, mostly citric); LI's table has no pineapple row; swept 8-13 g and 0.5-1.0%

white_wine_dry_california_bay.name: dry California white wine (crisp, unoaked, dry Riesling style), one dried bay leaf left in the bottle overnight in the fridge
white_wine_dry_california_bay.source: unsourced standard values (own knowledge): dry California whites run ~12-13.5% ABV, dry = under ~4 g/L residual sugar, titratable acid ~0.6-0.75%; swept 11.5-14% and 0-0.9 g in the room. Bay: scent and a little taste, no sugar, acid or strength (craft call); kitchen bay (laurel) touches no studio veto. Wine fining ignored (no named bottle)

rum_virgin_islands.source: unsourced: 40% typical; style from Duffy's Herald Punch (Imbibe! pdf 92, 'St. Croix')

orange_juice_sharpened.source: derived by Tomás from Liquid Intelligence p. 60 (Lime Acid Orange: 1 L orange juice, 32 g citric, 20 g malic, to lime strength) and the p. 137 table (orange juice 12.4% sugar, 0.8% acid): 22 g acids per litre adds about 2.2%, so 0.8 + 2.2 = 3.0% acid

grappa.name: young grappa (giovane or bianco, not wood-aged; Italian pomace brandy, 40%)

red_wine_nebbiolo.name: dry young Nebbiolo red wine (Langhe Nebbiolo style)

nebbiolo_syrup.source: computed by Tomás from red_wine_nebbiolo (LI dry-red sugar/acid, ABV 14% unsourced) + 250 g sugar at LI's 0.62 ml/g (p. 51): 250 g / ~405 ml; ABV is the pre-warming ceiling, some alcohol leaves on warming (unsourced)

strawberry_muddled.name: fresh strawberries, muddled (counted as the juice they give: 2 medium strawberries about 15 ml)
strawberry_muddled.source: Liquid Intelligence ingredient table, strawberry juice 8% sugar, 1.50% acid (pdf 141, printed 137); yield per berry unsourced (my estimate, swept 10-20 ml)

cucumber_muddled.name: cucumber slices, muddled (counted as the juice they give: 3 thin slices about 8 ml)
cucumber_muddled.source: unsourced standard values (my knowledge: cucumber is mostly water, ~1.7 g sugar/100 g, very low acid; Flavor Matrix pdf 100: high water content, mildest flavour); yield unsourced

sanbitter.name: Sanbitter (San Pellegrino), recommended, or any non-alcoholic Italian bitter aperitif soda
sanbitter.source: named in the Gunshop Fizz (A Proper Drink p. 289). Sugar ~10 g/100 ml and acid ~0.3% unsourced (typical sweetened soft drink; swept 6-13 g); non-alcoholic

mint_sprig_clapped.name: fresh mint sprig, clapped once between the hands and set in the glass
mint_sprig_clapped.source: a single clap releases the aroma without crushing or tearing (Oxford SPANKING FOR AROMATIZED GARNISHES, pdf 1853, Maloney's technique); pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 100, cucumber best pairings include mint; scent, not modelled

pimms_no1.name: Pimm's No. 1 Cup, recommended, or any gin-based fruit cup (about 25%)

malt_rich_syrup.source: computed: rich syrup 89 g/100 ml (LI p. 51) x2/3 + barley malt syrup ~84 g sugars/100 ml (unsourced: ~60% sugars by mass x ~1.4 g/ml) x1/3 = 87; maltose reads less sweet than sucrose (unsourced), so dosed at the full end; undistilled malt -> gluten (studio rule)
