scotch_blended_saffron.source: = blended scotch (LI pdf 140 note, 40% label); saffron adds aroma and colour only, no sugar, acid or strength; Oxford INFUSION pdf 1072: saffron infused in alcohol gives a yellow colour; dose and time unsourced craft call

old_potrero_rye.name: Old Potrero Straight Rye whiskey (48.5%; 100% rye malt, copper pot still), recommended; the Toasted Barrel bottling (51.2%) also works
old_potrero_rye.source: 48.5% Straight Rye 6YO and 51.2% Toasted Barrel 6YO: oldpotrero.com, read by Hester (outlaw-ruler r2); 100 percent malted rye: Oxford ANCHOR DISTILLING pdf 103; distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

quince_paste_loosened.name: quince paste (membrillo), loosened 1:1 by weight with just-boiled water, mashed until no lumps are left
quince_paste_loosened.source: UNSOURCED Tomás estimate: shop membrillo about 55-65 g sugar per 100 g, halved by the 1:1 loosening (~30 g/100 ml); fruit acid ~0.3%; swept 25-35 g and 0-1% acid. nuts on the safe side: the same paste is sold with walnuts mixed in (membrillo con nueces) and is packed and served alongside nuts, the dried-fruit call (row apricot_steeped_rye)

sherry_vinegar.name: sherry vinegar (vinagre de Jerez)
sherry_vinegar.source: unsourced standard values: acidity ~7% acetic (my knowledge of the Jerez minimum for the basic grade; aged grades run higher); sugar ~1 g/100 ml estimate. Wine vinegar: fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4); sulphites are not a veto

bourbon_cask_strength.name: cask-strength (barrel-proof) bourbon, about 60%
bourbon_cask_strength.source: unsourced standard value: cask-strength bourbons are bottled undiluted, commonly ~55-68% (my knowledge; swept 55-68); straight spirit, no sugar or acid (LI pdf 140 note); distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4). Oxford AMARETTO SOUR pdf 97 (Morgenthaler) calls for 'good cask-strength bourbon'

tarragon_leaves.name: fresh tarragon leaves (French tarragon), shaken with the drink and fine-strained out
tarragon_leaves.source: herb leaf shaken with the drink and fine-strained out; scent and a little taste, no sugar, acid or strength; not modelled in balance. Pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 270 (citrus-aroma compounds such as limonene, myrcene and citronellol are also found in many herbs, especially basil, sage, mint, tarragon); gin, lemon and tarragon together in the Little Dragon (Joy of Mixology pdf 323-324). Leaf herb, no heat: no veto

tarragon_sprig_clapped.name: fresh tarragon sprig, clapped once between the hands and set in the glass
tarragon_sprig_clapped.source: a single clap releases the aroma without crushing or tearing (Oxford SPANKING FOR AROMATIZED GARNISHES, pdf 1853); scent, not modelled; leaf herb, no heat: no veto

popcorn_demerara_syrup.name: popcorn syrup (100 g demerara sugar dissolved in 100 ml hot water; off the heat, 20 g plain popcorn popped in a dry lidded pan, no oil, butter or salt, stirred in, covered 30 minutes, pressed through a sieve; about 120 ml, fridge, a week)
popcorn_demerara_syrup.source: sugar as LI demerara syrup (ingredient table pdf 140-141, pp. 136-137); the popcorn adds toasted-corn aroma and flavour, its own sugar and the liquid it holds back not measured (unsourced). Veto-free as made here: home-popped plain kernels; bought popcorn can carry butter (dairy) or coconut oil (nuts)

ice_water.name: ice-cold still water (poured from a jug of water and ice, measured, no ice in the drink)
ice_water.source: plain water; the dilution step of Liquid Intelligence p. 152 (booze in the freezer, dilute with ice water at the last minute)

fortaleza_blanco.name: Fortaleza Blanco tequila (40%)
fortaleza_blanco.source: label ABV 40% (unsourced; Hester to confirm); straight spirit: no sugar, minimal acid (Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note)

oregano_sprig_pinched.name: small fresh oregano sprig, pinched once between finger and thumb and laid on the ice
oregano_sprig_pinched.source: garnish: scent, not modelled; leaf herb, no heat, so no spice veto (spice = heat only). Pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 306 (tequila shares carvacrol with papaya; oregano also carries it)

genever_oude.name: oude (old-style) genever (style: Dutch or Belgian genever with at least 15% malt wine; 35% or stronger)
genever_oude.source: Oxford GENEVER pdf 875: oude style must contain at least 15% moutwijn, be at least 35% ABV, and contain no more than 20 g sugar per litre (so 0-2 g/100 ml; row at the 1.0 midpoint, swept 0-2); pdf 870: oude genever is closest in flavour to a whisky, juniper not traditionally dominant. Distilled grain spirit (moutwijn from rye, corn and malted barley, pdf 874): not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4). ABV row at the legal floor; bottles commonly run higher (unsourced), swept 35-42.

rye_barrel_proof.name: barrel-proof (cask-strength) straight rye whiskey, about 60%
rye_barrel_proof.source: unsourced standard value: barrel-proof straight ryes are bottled undiluted, commonly ~55-68% (my knowledge; swept 55-68, as bourbon_cask_strength); straight spirit, no sugar or acid (LI pdf 140 note); distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4). Plan row sage-hero (plans/sage.md): a style, no named bottle

coffee_ice_block.name: one large block of ice frozen from ordinary black coffee (filter or cafetiere, no sugar, no milk), cooled before freezing
coffee_ice_block.source: garnish kind: not modelled at serve, because the drink is stirred on ordinary ice and strained over the block, so its melt arrives after serving (meltwater layers round a large cube and barely mixes until swirled, LI p. 112, pdf 116). Its melt is modelled separately in Checks with the hot_coffee row's values (no sugar, acid ~0.1, unsourced). Coffee touches no studio veto (no nuts, dairy, gluten, egg or heat), as coffee_beans_whole. Freezes outside-in, centre last, with dissolved matter pushed toward the centre (LI pp. 67-69, pdf 71-73, about impurities; applying it to coffee solids is my inference)

verjus_blanc.name: white verjus (verjus blanc: juice pressed from wine grapes before they ripen, unfermented)
verjus_blanc.source: What it is: Cocktail Codex p. 187 (VERJUS box). Grapes' acids are tartaric and malic: Liquid Intelligence p. 61 (pdf 65). Sugar 6 g/100 ml and acid 2.5% are unsourced standard values (no book gives verjus numbers), swept 3-10 g and 1.5-3.5% in sage-innocent. Allergens: unfermented grape juice, none of the five vetoes

tartaric_acid_solution.name: tartaric acid solution (10 g tartaric acid powder in 100 g water)
tartaric_acid_solution.source: Cocktail Codex p. 195 (TARTARIC ACID: make a 10-to-1 solution, as for malic); 9.1% = 10 g in 110 g total, by weight. Acid swaps gram for gram: Liquid Intelligence p. 58. Home-brew shops sell the acid: Liquid Intelligence p. 378 (via Hester, sage-innocent r2)

raspberry_red_wine_syrup.name: raspberry and red wine syrup (100 g fresh raspberries, 100 g white sugar and 100 ml dry young red wine, Cabernet Sauvignon style; blended cold until the sugar has gone, left 30 minutes, pressed through a fine sieve to take out the seeds; fridge, up to a week; adapted from the Cocktail Codex's Blended Strawberry Syrup, p. 47)
raspberry_red_wine_syrup.source: derived: the raspberry_syrup row's basis (100 g raspberries + 100 g sugar ~ 157 ml sieved, 66.5 g/100 ml, 1.0% acid; raspberry values unsourced) + 100 ml dry red as LI's Cabernet row (14.5%, 0.2 g, 0.55%, pdf 140-141) = ~257 ml: 104.6 g sugar -> 40.7 g/100 ml; 1.57 + 0.55 g acid -> 0.82%; 14.5 ml ethanol -> 5.6% (no heat, so none lost). Wine fining ignored (no named bottle)

port_ruby.name: ruby port (young, non-vintage)
port_ruby.source: style: Cocktail Codex p. 250 (ruby: non-vintage, at least two years in wood; port fortified to at least 17.5%). ABV 19.5%, sugar ~10 g/100 ml and acid ~0.5% are unsourced standard values (typical ruby labels 19-20%, ~90-110 g/L residual sugar); swept 8.5-13 g in the pour's checks. Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4)

port_tawny_10.name: 10-year-old tawny port
port_tawny_10.source: style: Cocktail Codex p. 250 (tawny: a blend of vintages, not for bottle ageing; older tawnies bring more structure). ABV 20%, sugar ~11.5 g/100 ml and acid ~0.5% are unsourced standard values (typical 10-year tawny labels 19.5-20%, ~100-130 g/L); swept in the pour's checks. Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4)

scotch_single_malt_highland_unpeated.name: unpeated Highland single malt Scotch whisky (bourbon-cask, no sherry or wine finish)
scotch_single_malt_highland_unpeated.source: Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note: straight spirits = label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid; 40% typical label (unsourced for the style), swept 40-46%

nikka_from_the_barrel.name: Nikka From the Barrel blended Japanese whisky (51.4%)
nikka_from_the_barrel.source: 51.4% label strength unsourced (Hester to check the label); straight spirit, no sugar, minimal acid (LI pdf 140 note). Distilled grain whisky (malt and grain), not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

japanese_blended_whisky.name: Japanese blended whisky (style), 40% or stronger
japanese_blended_whisky.source: style floor 40% (common label strength, unsourced); straight spirit (LI pdf 140 note); distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

egg_whole_lavender.name: whole egg (one large, raw), kept overnight in its shell beside dried culinary lavender (Codex p. 94 egg infusion)
egg_whole_lavender.source: ~50 ml per large egg (egg_white ~30 ml + egg_yolk ~17 ml rows, unsourced standard); the shell infusion adds aroma only (Codex p. 253: the white absorbs the aroma through the semipermeable shell), no sugar, acid or strength. The veto enum's only egg entry is 'egg-white': a whole egg contains it. Lavender is on no veto list

jasmine_tea_syrup.name: jasmine tea syrup (1:1: plain jasmine green tea, brewed strong and strained, equal weight of white sugar dissolved in)
jasmine_tea_syrup.source: sugar as 1:1 simple syrup, Liquid Intelligence ingredient table (pp. 136-137); tea adds no measurable sugar or acid (as rum_aged_tea row); plain jasmine-scented green tea, no other flavourings: tea is on no veto list

shochu_barley.name: barley shochu (honkaku, single-distilled; a style, about 25%)
shochu_barley.source: Shochu among Ikeda's Japanese ingredients at Angel's Share: A Proper Drink pp. 48-49. Strength: Oxford Companion SHOCHU pdf 1784-1786, 'usually 25%' (via Hester, lover-magician r2), swept 20-30%; Oxford divides it into neutral (korui) and aromatic pot-still (honkaku); in US shops it's often mislabelled 'soju', and Korean soju is a different spirit. Sugar/acid: straight distilled spirit (Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note). A distilled grain spirit, so not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); rice shochu the same

shiso_leaf.name: fresh green shiso leaf (perilla leaf, ooba)
shiso_leaf.source: Herb leaf stirred with the drink and strained out; not modelled in balance (scent and a little taste; no sugar, acid or strength). Shiso leaf among Ikeda's Japanese ingredients: A Proper Drink p. 49. Pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 288 lists juniper and shiso together among the things that share alpha-pinene (cedar, pine, resin, sharp); pdf 286 lists shiso among those sharing anethole (anise, sweet). Allergens: a mint-family leaf (my knowledge, unsourced), not a nut, not heat; the leaf, never the seed

scotch_single_grain.name: single grain Scotch whisky (style; column-distilled, usually from maize or wheat), 40% or stronger
scotch_single_grain.source: Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note: straight spirits = label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid; 40% = legal Scotch floor (unsourced here). Style per Oxford WHISKY, GRAIN pdf 2149 (corn or soft winter wheat, malted barley added). Distilled grain spirit: not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

scotch_single_grain_46.name: single grain Scotch whisky at 46% (strength sweep)
scotch_single_grain_46.source: sweep value for the style's stronger bottlings (unsourced)

calvados.name: calvados (AOC Calvados, the plain appellation)
calvados.source: Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note: straight spirits = label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid; 40% typical label (unsourced). Oxford CALVADOS pdf 389: cider-based brandy

egg_whole.name: whole egg (one large, raw)
egg_whole.source: ~50 ml per large egg (egg_white ~30 ml + egg_yolk ~17 ml rows, unsourced standard); the veto enum's only egg entry is 'egg-white': a whole egg contains it

beef_broth_homemade.name: plain beef broth, made at home (beef shin and bones simmered in water with onion and carrot; no salt, pepper, celery or stock cube; skimmed, not clarified)
beef_broth_homemade.source: values unsourced (home broth: no alcohol, a trace of sugar from the onion and carrot, no titratable acid). Oxford BULLSHOT pdf 375: DeGroff's recipe allows canned or house-made broth. Allergens: beef, bones, water, onion, carrot only, no veto touched; made at home so no yeast extract, hydrolysed wheat protein, milk powder or egg-white clarification (cf. beef_broth_canned). Gelatin from the bones is not a veto. Not vegetarian (no veto).

sherry_medium_dry.name: medium dry sherry (an amontillado-style sherry with a little sweetness)
sherry_medium_dry.source: unsourced standard values: medium dry sherries run about 17-18% with a few grams of sugar per 100 ml (my estimate; swept 0.2-5 g); acid as the amontillado row. Named in DeGroff's Bullshot (Oxford BULLSHOT pdf 375). Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4)

aperol.name: Aperol, recommended, or any bright orange Italian bitter aperitivo of about 11%
aperol.source: ABV 11%: Cocktail Codex p. 258 ('At 11% ABV, Aperol is the lightest of all aperitivi bitters'); Oxford APEROL pdf 125: 11-15% depending on market (swept). Botanicals per Oxford pdf 125: oranges, cinchona, rhubarb, gentian (recipe not published; no nut or heat on record, so none, as Campari's row). Sugar UNSOURCED estimate 26 g/100 ml, swept 18-34

amaro_nonino.name: Amaro Nonino Quintessentia (35%), recommended, or any grappa-based amaro
amaro_nonino.source: ABV 35%: Cocktail Codex p. 259 ('high in proof (35% ABV) but not too sweet'; grappa base; orange oil, herbs, birch). Sugar 20.8 g/100 ml: Alko (Finnish state retailer) listing, 208 g/l, a LEAD from a search summary, page not read (Hester, innocent-jester r3); swept with Aperol 18-34. Allergens: spice, on the safe side (Tomás, innocent-jester r4, on his own row from r2): the same unread summary lists galangal among the botanicals (with caramelised sugar, bitter and sweet orange, cinchona, gentian, liquorice, quassia, rhubarb, saffron, tamarind); the Flavor Matrix puts galangal in ginger's family and lists it as ginger's substitute (pdf 132), and this studio files ginger under spice (gingerol 'a relative of capsaicin', pdf 132). No nut or nutmeg listed. | RULED none (Robin 2026-10-06, collection review D1/D8): a row is classed only on a stated ingredient (a published ingredient list, the maker's declaration, a 'may contain' label on the recommended bottle, or a book naming the ingredient), never on a tasting note, a rumoured historical formula or 'secret recipe' alone; the earlier safe-side reasoning is kept above for the record. Basis here: galangal only in an unread search summary.

orgeat_toasted_almond.name: toasted almond orgeat, made at home (150 g blanched almonds toasted in the oven at 180°C for 8-10 minutes until pale gold, cooled, blended with 300 ml water, left 30 minutes, squeezed through a clean cloth; the almond milk weighed and warmed gently with the same weight of white sugar until dissolved, never boiled; off the heat, 1/4 teaspoon orange flower water; about 400 ml, fridge, up to 2 weeks)
orgeat_toasted_almond.source: computed: 1:1 by weight almond milk and sugar (sugar 0.62 ml/g, LI p. 51) -> ~61.7 g/100 ml, same basis as LI's orgeat row (pp. 136-137); the almond milk's own sugar and fat ignored (unsourced, small). Method after Codex House Orgeat p. 285 (almond milk and sugar warmed until dissolved); toasting per Flavor Matrix pdf 184 (nuts toasted to bring out flavour; Maillard); orange flower water per Oxford ORGEAT pdf 1451. Almonds: nuts.

rum_appleton_12.name: Appleton Estate 12 Year Old Rare Casks Jamaica rum (43%), recommended, or any aged Jamaican rum, the oldest you can find
rum_appleton_12.source: label 43% (unsourced: Hester checks the label); sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note; Appleton Estate part of J. Wray and Nephew since the early 20th century (Oxford APPLETON ESTATE RUM pdf 132), the firm whose seventeen-year rum Vic used (Oxford MAI TAI pdf 1211); 'substitute the oldest Jamaican available' (pdf 1212)

lime_shell_half.name: half the squeezed lime shell, dropped in
lime_shell_half.source: Vic's 1970 telling via Joy of Mixology pdf 327 ('Half the lime shell went in for color'); Oxford MAI TAI pdf 1212 ('a spent lime shell'); scent only, juice counted in lime_juice

mint_branch.name: a big branch of fresh mint, standing up out of the ice
mint_branch.source: Vic's 1970 telling via Joy pdf 327 ('a branch of fresh mint'); Oxford MAI TAI pdf 1212 (mint); scent only

folle_blanche_armagnac.name: young Armagnac made from Folle Blanche (single-grape, labelled Folle Blanche; unaged blanche or young; 40% or stronger)
folle_blanche_armagnac.source: Oxford ARMAGNAC pdf 139 (Folle Blanche: floral and fruity spirit, best young); pdf 138 (blanche Armagnac, unaged, a category since 2005); 40% label floor unsourced, swept 40-50%; LI pdf 140 note: straight spirits, no sugar, minimal acid

gooseberry_syrup.name: blended gooseberry syrup (2 parts fresh or frozen green gooseberries to 1 part white sugar by weight, blended cold until smooth, pressed through a fine sieve; fridge, up to a week; adapted from the Cocktail Codex's Blended Strawberry Syrup, p. 47, at half its sugar)
gooseberry_syrup.source: method adapted from Codex p. 47 (Blended Strawberry Syrup: equal weights fruit and sugar, blended cold, sieved); here 2 fruit : 1 sugar, Tomás's own adaptation. Values UNSOURCED estimate by Tomás: gooseberry ~6 g sugar/100 g, ~1.8% titratable acid; 200 g fruit ~190 ml + 100 g sugar ~62 ml (LI 0.62 ml/g, pp. 136-137) = ~252 ml -> ~44 g sugar/100 ml, ~1.4% acid; swept 38-50 g and 1.0-1.8%. Matrix GRAPES pdf 140 lists gooseberries among grape substitutes. Allergens: fresh berry (Ribes), no veto class; not the cape gooseberry (physalis)

wormwood_tangerine_bitters.name: wormwood bitters made at home (about 10 g dried wormwood and the thin-cut peel of one tangerine, steeped 2 days in 250 ml overproof white rum of about 63%, strained)
wormwood_tangerine_bitters.source: Method: Imbibe! pdf 124-125 (Wondrich: 5-6 sprigs or 1 oz dried wormwood plus the thin-cut peels of three tangerines, a tip from Eleanor Early's Ports of the Sun, 1937, in a 750 ml bottle of navy-strength gin or overproof white rum, a couple of days, strained), scaled to a third by Tomas. ABV 60%: unsourced estimate (63% spirit, a little lost to the herb and peel), swept 50-63%. No sugar or acid added. Allergens none, Tomas's call: wormwood is a herb (Asteraceae), tangerine peel a citrus peel, rum a distilled spirit; none touches egg, dairy, gluten, nuts or heat.

swizzle_stick_left_in.name: wooden swizzle stick, left standing in the glass
swizzle_stick_left_in.source: Oxford SWIZZLE pdf 1963 (the stick rolled between the palms); left in the glass: Wren's ruling, jester-innocent r3. A tool, no flavour.

absinthe_verte_tangerine.name: green absinthe (verte, a wormwood-forward style, about 68%), steeped two days with the thin-cut peel of one tangerine per 100 ml, strained
absinthe_verte_tangerine.source: Absinthe: distilled with grand wormwood, aniseed and fennel; the green from chlorophyll in the finishing herbs (Oxford ABSINTHE pdf 50); 'wormwood-forward' absinthe as the stand-in for home-steeped wormwood bitters in the Green Swizzle (Imbibe! pdf 125). Tangerine peel: Eleanor Early's 1937 tip for the wormwood bitters, credited by Wondrich (Imbibe! pdf 125); putting it in the absinthe is Tomas's adaptation (jester-innocent r4), replacing the undistilled home wormwood steep, for which no page gives a safe thujone level (Oxford pdf 50, 2212; Hester r3). ABV 68% as the table's generic absinthe (unsourced standard value, labels 45-74%), swept 45-74%; peel adds no sugar or acid. Allergens none: a distilled spirit and citrus peel.

amaro_ciociaro.name: Amaro CioCiaro (30%), recommended, or any dark, bittersweet Italian amaro with a burnt-orange character, about 30%
amaro_ciociaro.source: Liquid Intelligence ingredient table pdf 140 (p. 136): Amaro CioCiaro 30.0% ABV, 16.0 g sugar/100 ml, 0.00% acid. Flavour: Cocktail Codex p. 260 (cola and orange aromas, burnt-orange flavour, moderate sweetness, 30%; 'a favorite substitute for Amer Picon in classics like the Brooklyn'); Oxford BROOKLYN COCKTAIL pdf 361 names it as the substitute in Grohusko's recipe. Allergens: recipe not published; no nut, nutmeg, dairy, egg, gluten or heat ingredient on any page read; classified veto-free on the Campari/Cynar precedent ('cola aromas' is a tasting note, not an ingredient). Substitute style swept for ABV and sugar in innocent-lover.

rum_jamaican_aged_50.name: aged Jamaican rum, about 50% (100 US proof), style; not spiced, not sweetened
rum_jamaican_aged_50.source: LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note (label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid). Strength after the Brooklyn Club's drink as the Brooklyn Eagle printed it, 13 Dec 1945 p. 3: half Jamaica rum (100 proof), half Italian vermouth, a dash of Angostura (Hester, innocent-lover anchors F17). Swept 40-63% in innocent-lover: 40-57% in range (57% edge), 63% OUT.

kirsch.name: kirsch (kirschwasser: clear, unsweetened cherry eau-de-vie)
kirsch.source: Oxford CAFÉ BRÛLOT pdf 381 (120 ml kirschwasser in the recipe). 40% typical bottling and 0 g sugar unsourced (clear eau-de-vie, as apricot_eau_de_vie); swept 40-45%. nuts on the safe side, same call as maraschino and apricot_eau_de_vie in this table: Oxford KIRSCHWASSER pdf 1135, 'distilled from cherries and their pits', with 'almond-like' flavours (Hester, jester-lover r2); Flavor Matrix pdf 304 lists benzaldehyde-bitter almond under CHERRY

coffee_chicory.name: hot brewed dark-roast coffee with chicory (New Orleans style, filter or cafetière, not espresso)
coffee_chicory.source: Oxford CAFÉ BRÛLOT pdf 381: 'French roast coffee flavored with chicory'. Values as hot_coffee (unsourced: no sugar, acid ~0.1 estimated); chicory root is roasted and ground in with the coffee and touches no studio veto (not nuts, dairy, gluten, egg or heat)

cinnamon_stick.name: cinnamon stick (steeped and removed)
cinnamon_stick.source: Oxford CAFÉ BRÛLOT pdf 381 (3 sticks, broken, marinated in the spirits). Aroma only, no sugar, acid or strength modelled (unsourced). A baking spice, not heat (STUDIO-RULES 4)

clove.name: whole clove (studded into an orange-peel spiral)
clove.source: Oxford CAFÉ BRÛLOT pdf 381 (12 cloves studded into a spiral orange peel). Aroma only, nothing measured (unsourced). A baking spice, not heat (STUDIO-RULES 4)

lark_classic_cask.name: Lark Classic Cask Tasmanian single malt whisky (43%), recommended, or any Tasmanian single malt
lark_classic_cask.source: 43% label strength unsourced (my knowledge; Hester to check the label). Straight spirit: no sugar, minimal acid (LI pdf 140 note). Distilled grain (malted barley) spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); cask fining ignored (no label claim)

pepperberry_water.name: Tasmanian pepperberry water (3 dried Tasmanian pepperberries, Tasmannia lanceolata, also sold as mountain pepper, lightly cracked with the back of a spoon, steeped in 100 ml cold still water in the fridge for 15 minutes, strained)
pepperberry_water.source: plain water; three dried berries add colour, aroma and some heat, no measurable sugar or acid at this dose (unsourced, my estimate). spice on the safe side: a native pepper whose heat a guest avoiding heat would reasonably fear (STUDIO-RULES 4: spice = heat)

gin_gordons.name: Gordon's London Dry gin (37.5%, UK bottling), recommended, or any London dry gin
gin_gordons.source: label ABV 37.5% for the UK bottling (unsourced, my knowledge; strength differs by market, ~40% elsewhere and 47.3% for some export bottlings: Hester checks the label); unsweetened London dry (LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note). Named because the Vesper's order names it (Oxford VESPER pdf 2099)

rum_jamaican_any.name: Jamaican rum (white or aged; not spiced, not sweetened), 40% or stronger
rum_jamaican_any.source: LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note (label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid); 40% typical label (unsourced), swept 40-63%. Style only: Oxford VESPER pdf 2099 says the name came from 'a curious drink of frozen rum with fruit and herbs' in Jamaica, with no rum named

johnnie_walker_red_label.name: Johnnie Walker Red Label blended Scotch whisky (40%), recommended, or any blended Scotch whisky
johnnie_walker_red_label.source: label ABV 40% (unsourced here; Hester to confirm for the guest's market); straight spirit, no sugar, minimal acid (LI pdf 140 note). Distilled grain spirit: not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); caramel colouring is no veto

strawberry_lemon_cordial.name: strawberry and lemon cordial (100 g ripe hulled strawberries blended cold with 100 g white sugar, pressed through a fine sieve; then the same volume of fresh lemon juice stirred in, about 300 ml; fridge, up to a week; syrup step after the Cocktail Codex's Blended Strawberry Syrup, p. 47)
strawberry_lemon_cordial.source: computed, unsourced: strawberries ~4.9 g sugar/100 g and ~0.7% acid (unsourced standard values); 100 g sugar ~62 ml (LI 0.62 ml/g); sieved syrup ~150 ml + 150 ml lemon juice (LI table: 1.6 g sugar, 6.0% acid) = ~300 ml -> (100+4.9+2.4)/300 = 35.8 g/100 ml; (0.7+9.0)/300 = 3.2% acid

glenfarclas_single_malt.name: Glenfarclas single malt Scotch whisky (recommended; or any Scotch single malt), 40% or stronger
glenfarclas_single_malt.source: 40% = Scotch legal floor, unsourced for the bottle (bottlings vary; swept 40-60%). Distillery in Scotland: SB 2022 (Hester F11). Straight spirit: no sugar, minimal acid (LI pdf 140 note). Distilled malted barley, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4); fining ignored (no label claim)

sharp_apple_slice.name: a thin slice of raw, sharp eating or cooking apple (the sharpest to hand, e.g. a crab apple or a Granny Smith style), skin on, cut just before serving
sharp_apple_slice.source: garnish only: a thin raw slice set in the glass, not modelled in balance (fresh apple; no veto: fruit, no nut, dairy, gluten, egg or heat)

sweet_vermouth_beet.name: sweet vermouth steeped with raw beetroot (50 g peeled raw beetroot, thinly sliced, per 250 ml sweet vermouth, room temperature, about 12 hours, strained, then kept in the fridge)
sweet_vermouth_beet.source: Tomás estimate, unsourced: base values sweet_vermouth (Liquid Intelligence pp. 136-137: 16.5%, 16 g, 0.6%); the slices take up some vermouth and give back beet water (raw beet ~88% water, ~7 g sugar per 100 g, my knowledge), so at about half-equilibrium the strained vermouth runs ~15% and ~15 g/100 ml; swept 14-16.5% and 14-17 g. Steep time after Cocktail Codex p. 95 (low-proof vermouth infuses slowly; St-Germain 20% ~12 h). Pairing: Flavor Matrix GRAPE pdf 140 lists beet among grape's surprising pairings. Beetroot: no veto (not a nut, grain, dairy, egg or heat).

lime_peel.name: lime peel (a wide strip cut from the same lime before it's juiced)
lime_peel.source: garnish only: oils squeezed over the top, not modelled in balance; citrus aroma lives in the zest's oils (Flavor Matrix pdf 80)

bourbon_beet.name: bourbon steeped with raw beetroot (60 g peeled raw beetroot, coarsely grated, per 250 ml bourbon, room temperature, about 30 minutes, tasted every few minutes, strained through a fine sieve lined with a coffee filter; fridge, a few days)
bourbon_beet.source: Tomás estimate, unsourced: base bourbon 45% (LI pdf 140 note, table row bourbon); the grated beet gives back some juice (raw beet ~88% water, ~7 g sugar per 100 g, my knowledge), so the strained spirit runs ~43.5% and under 1 g sugar per 100 ml; swept 40-45% and 0-2 g. Room-temperature steep for a fast-infusing ingredient, tasted often: Cocktail Codex p. 94. Pairing: Flavor Matrix COCOA pdf 84 lists beet among cocoa's surprise pairings and whiskey among its best. Beetroot and bourbon: no veto (beet is not a nut, grain, dairy, egg or heat; distilled grain spirit is not gluten).

rum_bacardi_carta_blanca.name: Bacardi Carta Blanca white rum (recommended; or any Cuban-style white rum)
rum_bacardi_carta_blanca.source: Oxford MARY PICKFORD pdf 1252 names Bacardi; ABV 37.5% is the lower common label (EU/UK), 40% in the US (unsourced: Hester checks the label); swept 37.5-40; sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note

pineapple_juice.name: fresh pineapple juice (or unsweetened, not-from-concentrate)
pineapple_juice.source: unsourced standard value for fresh pineapple juice (~10 g sugar/100 ml, ~0.8% acid, mostly citric), as pineapple_juice_pressed; LI's table has no pineapple row; swept 8-13 g and 0.5-1.0%

thyme_grenadine.name: thyme grenadine, made at home (250 g pomegranate juice, 250 g sugar, 6 thyme sprigs lightly crushed; shaken in a jar until the sugar dissolves, no heat; overnight in the fridge, strained; about 400 ml, a week or two in the fridge)
thyme_grenadine.source: Method: Codex House Grenadine (equal weights pomegranate juice and cane sugar, cold), without its acid powders and orange extract; values as pomegranate_syrup (computed, unsourced). Thyme: Flavor Matrix pdf 248 (tropical fruit best pairing); steeps out, adds no sugar, acid or strength; overnight cold steep is a craft call (unsourced)

rum_white_50.name: white rum, 50% or stronger (unaged or lightly aged, not spiced, not sweetened; style)
rum_white_50.source: LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note (label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid); 50% is the floor the sweep sets for lover-ruler, swept 50-63%

underberg.name: Underberg (German herbal digestif bitters, 44%, sold in 20 ml single-serve bottles), recommended, or any German-style herbal digestif bitters (Kräuterbitter)
underberg.source: Named on A Proper Drink p. 237 (LeNell stocked Underberg bitters, 'considered food products'); Joy of Mixology pdf 419 gives it as the example of a digestif. ABV 44% and the 20 ml bottle: label, my knowledge, unsourced in the library (Hester to confirm). Sugar 0: unsourced placeholder for an unsweetened herbal bitters, swept 0-10 g/100 ml (moves nothing at 5 ml). Allergens: nuts on the safe side, Tomás's call: secret recipe of many herbs and spices, no published botanical list read; a herbal bitters may carry nutmeg (the Bénédictine lesson, Oxford pdf 256), so it counts until a source lists its botanicals. Spice: no heat expected (baking spices don't count). Distilled base: not gluten. | RULED none (Robin 2026-10-06, collection review D1/D8): a row is classed only on a stated ingredient (a published ingredient list, the maker's declaration, a 'may contain' label on the recommended bottle, or a book naming the ingredient), never on a tasting note, a rumoured historical formula or 'secret recipe' alone; the earlier safe-side reasoning is kept above for the record. Basis here: secret recipe only.

sorghum_syrup.name: sorghum syrup (pure, boiled down from the pressed juice of sorghum stalks; not a blend with corn syrup)
sorghum_syrup.source: Flavor Matrix pdf 240 (printed 230): sorghum syrup is made like cane syrup, from juiced sorghum, boiled down; Sugar Syrup best pairings include grain. Sugar ~90 g/100 ml: unsourced estimate (~65% sugars by mass x ~1.39 g/ml), swept 75-100. Acid ~0.3%: unsourced (a slight tang), swept 0-1. Allergens none: the pressed juice of sorghum stalks, boiled (Oxford SORGHUM pdf 1834; sorghum is a grass of the same subfamily as sugar cane, not cane); not malt, not the grain; no nut, dairy, egg or heat

apollinaris.name: Apollinaris sparkling mineral water (German; recommended), or any sparkling mineral water with a noticeable mineral taste
apollinaris.source: Oxford RICKEY pdf 1663: Col. Rickey's preferred water was reportedly Apollinaris. Values: unsourced standard (unsweetened, unflavoured mineral water: no alcohol, no sugar; dissolved CO2 not counted as titratable acid, as soda_water). Codex p. 211: mineral waters vary by source; minerals brighten citrus (said of soda water's added minerals). No allergen: water, minerals, CO2

banane_du_bresil.name: Giffard Banane du Brésil banana liqueur (25%), recommended, or any crème de banane (banana liqueur, about 25%)
banane_du_bresil.source: Codex p. 35 (Bananarac: 'balanced and characterized by a true banana flavor'); ABV 25% from the label (unsourced here, Hester to confirm); sugar 25 g/100 ml unsourced standard value for banana liqueurs, swept 20-35

lemon_zest_grated.name: lemon zest, finely grated over the drink (the yellow only)
lemon_zest_grated.source: garnish on the drink, no measurable sugar, acid or strength (unsourced, my call); citrus flavour sits in the zest's oils (Flavor Matrix pdf 80)

pear_syrup.name: fresh pear syrup (equal weights chopped ripe pear and white sugar, left overnight in the fridge, strained through a coffee filter)
pear_syrup.source: computed, unsourced: macerated 1:1 by weight fruit and sugar reads close to LI simple syrup (61.5 g/100 ml, pdf 140-141); pear's own acid (~0.2-0.4%, malic, unsourced) halved by the sugar; swept 50-70 g and 0-0.2%. Method after Codex p. 47 (fruit and sugar in equal weights, cold), as the tomato syrup. Pear flesh only, no seeds pressed: veto-free (fresh fruit; Tomás's call)

mint_leaves_pressed_out.name: fresh mint leaves (spearmint), pressed round the inside of the cup with the back of a spoon, then taken out
mint_leaves_pressed_out.source: the ode's method (1907 Morning Star printing, via Hester): mint crushed round the glass, then thrown away; Codex p. 30-31 rubs the tin with the bouquet and sets it aside. Leaves oil on the cup: scent and a little taste, no sugar, acid or strength; not modelled in balance

mint_bouquet.name: a tight bouquet of 4-5 fresh mint sprigs (spearmint), set in the ice beside the straw
mint_bouquet.source: Codex p. 30-31 (bouquet trimmed, set in the crushed ice by the straw); scent only

cognac_black_tea.name: cognac steeped with black tea (2 ordinary black-tea bags in 150 ml cognac, 20 minutes at room temperature, bags lifted out without squeezing)
cognac_black_tea.source: cognac as LI (41%); steep time after LI pp. 268-269 (Arnold's tea vodka, 32 g per litre, 20-40 min, which he then milk-washes to strip astringency; ours is not washed, keeps the tannin, so shorter and tasted: Cocktail Codex p. 94, black tea turns tannic if overextracted). ~30 g/L assumes ~2 g per bag (unsourced). Tea adds colour and tannin, no measurable sugar or acid; spirit lost in the bags ignored (as rum_aged_tea). Plain unflavoured black tea (Camellia sinensis): no veto; flavoured blends are not this row

batavia_arrack.name: Batavia arrack (Indonesian sugar-cane and rice spirit, from Java; not Sri Lankan coconut arrack), recommended; or a full-flavoured Jamaican-style rum, 50% or stronger
batavia_arrack.source: Oxford ARRACK, BATAVIA pdf 147-150: molasses and rice (palm sap once, since dropped, pdf 150), 'over 50 percent ABV' (pdf 149); 50% bottling unsourced (Hester checks the label); sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note. Allergens: nuts on the safe side, see why | RULED none (Robin 2026-10-06, collection review D1/D8): a row is classed only on a stated ingredient (a published ingredient list, the maker's declaration, a 'may contain' label on the recommended bottle, or a book naming the ingredient), never on a tasting note, a rumoured historical formula or 'secret recipe' alone; the earlier safe-side reasoning is kept above for the record. Basis here: palm sap said by Oxford pdf 150 to have left the formula, and no page names the palm.
batavia_arrack.why: safe side (Tomás, magician-ruler r4): Imbibe! pdf 66 says Batavia arrack is still made with 'a little bit of palm sap' (Oxford pdf 150 says it fell out; same author); no page names the palm, and coconut is a palm (coconut arrack is nuts). Open for Robin: his distillation rule may clear it

seville_palm_shrub.name: Seville-orange shrub with palm sugar (peel of 1 Seville orange rubbed into 90 g grated palm sugar, covered about 12 hours; then 250 ml fresh Seville orange juice stirred in until dissolved, strained, bottled; fridge, up to ten days; about 300 ml. Out of season: peel of 1 ordinary orange, 75 ml orange juice and 175 ml lemon juice)
seville_palm_shrub.source: computed by Tomás (v3, round 3: 90 g palm sugar) on the out-of-season juice (LI table pdf 140-141: orange 12.4 g / 0.8%, lemon 1.6 g / 6.0%): 88.6 g sugar, 11.1 g acid in ~307 ml; palm sugar ~85% sugar (unsourced, swept 75-95) at 0.63 ml/g. Seville juice: ~4.5% acid, 12.4 g sugar, back-calculated by Tomás from LI p. 175 (The Flat Leaf's printed 7.9 g / 0.82% with 30 ml sour orange juice; Arnold: Sevilles are a sour orange with 'relatively non-bitter juice') -> Seville shrub ~35.1 g / 3.67%, swept 4.0-5.0% juice acid. Oleo method and ten-day keeping: Oxford OLEO-SACCHARUM pdf 1440-1441. Pairing: Flavor Matrix pdf 240. Allergens: palm sugar is often coconut-palm sugar, so nuts on the safe side

seville_demerara_shrub.name: Seville-orange shrub with demerara sugar (peel of 1 Seville orange rubbed into 80 g demerara sugar, covered about 12 hours; then 250 ml fresh Seville orange juice stirred in until dissolved, strained, bottled; fridge, up to ten days; about 300 ml. Out of season: peel of 1 ordinary orange, 75 ml orange juice and 175 ml lemon juice)
seville_demerara_shrub.source: computed by Tomás (round 4) on the out-of-season juice (LI table pdf 140-141: orange 12.4 g / 0.8%, lemon 1.6 g / 6.0%) + 80 g demerara (100% sugar, 0.63 ml/g): 92.1 g sugar, 11.1 g acid in ~300 ml. Seville version on Arnold's sour-orange figure (LI pdf 141: 4.50% acid, 12.3% sugar; Sevilles not measured, p. 175): ~36.9 g / 3.75%, swept 4.0-5.0% acid. Oleo method and ten-day keeping: Oxford OLEO-SACCHARUM pdf 1440-1441

makrut_lime_leaf.name: makrut (kaffir) lime leaf, fresh or frozen, torn in half, pressed into the lime and sugar, lifted out before pouring
makrut_lime_leaf.source: Cocktail Codex p. 117 (common citrus table, LIMES: Kaffir and Makrut, a different lime from the juicing ones; 'Fragrant leaves are great for muddling and infusions'); scent only (Oxford GARNISH pdf 865: such leaves may work only on the nose), no sugar, acid or strength; not modelled in balance

grappa_nonino_monovitigno.name: Nonino single-varietal grappa (monovitigno; young, not wood-aged), recommended, or any young, not wood-aged single-varietal grappa, 40% or stronger
grappa_nonino_monovitigno.source: What it is: Oxford GRAPPA pdf 936 (Giannola Nonino, the first single varietal, from fresh lightly pressed pomace) and POLI, JACOPO pdf 1544 (Nonino's monovitigno). Young grappa rests at least six months, usually in steel or glass (Oxford GRAPPA pdf 935). Nonino's young single-varietal on record is the Picolit Cru (house page, Hester 2026-10-04). ABV 41% unsourced (no page gives a strength); swept 37.5-48%. Straight spirit: no sugar, minimal acid (Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note). Distilled from grape: no veto.

blanc_vermouth_fig_leaf.name: blanc vermouth (French style, e.g. Dolin Blanc) steeped with a fresh fig leaf (1 medium leaf, torn in 3-4 pieces, per 200 ml, room temperature, about 1 hour, leaf lifted out; fridge)
blanc_vermouth_fig_leaf.source: Values as blanc_vermouth (Liquid Intelligence pdf 140-141, Dolin Blanc); the leaf adds aroma only, no sugar, acid or strength (unsourced, not modelled). Fig leaves 'highly aromatic' and wrapped round food to give flavour: Flavor Matrix FIG pdf 120. Room-temperature infusion for quick ingredients, generally an hour or less, tasted as it goes: Cocktail Codex p. 94. A fresh leaf, not dried fruit: no veto (fig is not a nut; the safe-side nuts rule covers dried fruit).
